item.title: Your walking speed may hold a clue to how long you’ll live, study suggests
item.description: A JAMA Network Open study of over 4,000 older adults found faster walking pace was linked to lower death risk over nearly 12 years of follow-up.
item.content:encoded:
The speed a person normally walks could offer a simple clue about their overall health and longevity, new research suggests.

A study published in JAMA Network Open followed 4,067 adults in the U.K., who were about 69 years old on average, to see whether their usual walking pace was linked to their risk of death over time.

Participants completed a short walking test at their normal pace and also wore a wrist activity tracker for nine days to capture their walking speed during everyday life.

FORGET THE GYM: A 30-SECOND TEST MAY BE ONE OF THE BEST INDICATORS OF LONGEVITY

Over nearly 12 years of follow-up, faster walking in both settings was linked to a lower risk of death, even after researchers accounted for other health and lifestyle factors. A total of 739 participants died during that period.

Beth Templin, a board-certified geriatric clinical specialist and CEO of HouseFit Physical Therapy & Fitness in St. Louis, said walking speed can offer a broader look at how well the body is functioning.

"In physical therapy, we call walking speed the 'sixth vital sign' because it's a snapshot of how well many body systems are working together," Templin, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Changes in walking speed can therefore offer clues about a person's health, according to the doctor.

"To walk briskly, you need strong legs, a healthy heart and lungs, good balance, and a brain and nervous system that can coordinate it all," she said.

"When walking speed starts to slip, it's often an early warning sign that one of those systems is declining, sometimes before anything shows up on a lab test," Templin added.

For older adults who want to improve their walking speed and overall fitness, simply taking more steps may not be enough.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"Build the engine, not just the habit," Templin advised. "Most people try to walk more, but speed comes from strength and balance."

The doctor suggested strengthening the legs with simple exercises, such as standing up from a chair without using the hands and doing heel raises while holding onto a counter.

She also recommended adding short bursts of faster walking. After warming up, a person could walk briskly for one minute, slow down for two minutes and then repeat, gradually increasing the faster periods.

The findings do not mean that simply walking faster will make someone live longer, experts noted.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"This study shows an association, not proof that walking faster by itself adds years," Templin reiterated.

The participants included in the study were generally healthier than the larger group, the researchers noted. There is also no single standard method for measuring everyday walking pace with wrist activity trackers.

More research is needed to determine whether the findings apply to other groups.

Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.

item.title: Private jet with 9 people on board crashes just miles from Mar-a-Lago
item.description: A small plane carrying nine people crashed and exploded in Palm Beach County, Florida, just miles from Mar-a-Lago.
item.content:encoded:
A private jet carrying nine people slammed into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday afternoon, erupting into a massive fireball around nine miles from Mar-a-Lago. 

In a statement, the Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) confirmed that the plane crashed in a residential area near Cresthaven, Florida, around 12:50 p.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1.

"Nine people were on board," the FAA said.

"The aircraft departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas.

 'WE THOUGHT WE WOULD DIE': PASSENGERS THROWN INTO CEILING DURING TERRIFYING FLIGH

"The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate. The NTSB will be in charge of the investigation and will provide all updates," the FAA added.

Emergency crews shut down Military Trail between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, warning the public to avoid the area.

"Aircraft Incident," Palm Beach County Fire Rescue said on X. "Avoid the area. This will be an extended incident."

Video shared on social media showed the aircraft dropping rapidly before an explosion sent smoke and flames into the air.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

item.title: Mike Waltz reveals Cuban diplomat shoved US staffer, slapped phone away in explosive UN clash
item.description: Mike Waltz says a Cuban diplomat shoved his staff member and slapped a phone away at the United Nations before Secretary Marco Rubio ordered the official expelled.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz recalled on "The Sunday Briefing" how a heated confrontation with Cuban officials nearly turned physical, alleging that one diplomat shoved a member of his staff and slapped a phone out of his hand before being expelled from the United States.

"I really thought it was about to go down," Waltz said, attributing the decision to "boot the guy" back to Cuba to Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

"The guy that we actually put on a one-way flight back to his crumbling country shoved one of my staff, slapped the phone out of his hand, was trying to bully the U.N. staff into cutting my microphone. Then, their foreign minister gets up out of his chair and rushes the podium."

Waltz was accusing Cuba's government of enriching its leaders while its people suffered during a speech on the floor of the U.N. General Assembly when Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla approached the podium and sought to interrupt his remarks.

RUBIO URGES CUBANS TO WORK WITH CIA TO BRING POLITICAL CHANGE TO COMMUNIST-RUN ISLAND

"If they'll do that on the floor of the U.N. in front of diplomats, in front of the world, imagine what they do to these the poor Cuban people behind closed doors," Waltz said.

He said he was holding up photos showing the deceased former Cuban President Fidel Castro's private island and luxury jet, as well as the Rolex watches, luxury vacations and yachts enjoyed by current regime leaders.

"They use the U.N., they try to use it to further their propaganda and blame us. We're not going to have it, and we smacked it down, almost literally."

SHOUTING MATCH ERUPTS AT UN AS CUBAN FOREIGN MINISTER MOVES TOWARD US AMBASSADOR'S PODIUM: 'BACK UP!'

To back up his claims, the ambassador pointed to Rubio's 100-page report titled "Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism," which accuses the Cuban government of running espionage and influence operations in America.

Waltz said the Cuban regime "has been exporting communism, their Marxist ideology, through leftist groups and current politicians right here in the United States" and blamed much of the unrest in America on "67 years of putting up with Havana."

He finished with a prediction about the future of the Caribbean nation.

"I think the Cuban people will see freedom on President Trump's watch, and I'll just leave it at that."

Fox News Digital's Alec Schemmel contributed to this report.

item.title: 'The Pitt' star Noah Wyle does 100 push-ups a day ‘come rain or come shine’ at 55
item.description: Noah Wyle reveals his daily push-ups routine and chin-up bar goal with his accountability partner while filming the demanding medical drama "The Pitt."
item.content:encoded:
Noah Wyle is sharing how he manages to stay fit while filming the hit medical drama, "The Pitt."

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 55-year-old actor shared what it means for the Cedar Sinai Board of Governors to honor the show with the Hollywood Leadership Award, and how he stays fit enough to keep up with filming the physically demanding HBO Max show.

"I have an accountability partner and a guy named Dash Land who's the on-set dresser and he and I do a hundred push-ups every day, come rain or come shine. That's the base," Wyle said about his fitness routine. "We try to add a little bit on top of that if we can, if we remember to. That's base. We also installed a chin-up bar recently. I have a goal to be, I'm going to embarrass myself, to do ten by the end of the season. I'm at six right now, solid six."

The actor stars in "The Pitt," an intense medical drama which follows emergency nurses and doctors over the course of one shift, with each episode showcasing one hour of a 12-hour shift.

NOAH WYLE, MATT DAMON, LEONARDO DICAPRIO STILL CAPTIVATING AUDIENCES WELL INTO THEIR 50S

Wyle portrays Dr. Robby on the show, who is the chief attending physician and head of the emergency department at the fictional Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center, and is dealing with the emotional toll years of working on the frontlines of medicine can take on a person.

When speaking to Veja+ in January, Wyle said that the cast has to "take very good care of ourselves" almost "out of necessity," because while filming they "work 14 hours a day, five days a week, for nine months straight."

WATCH HERE: NOAH WYLE WORKS OUT EVERYDAY ON THE SET OF ‘THE PITT’ WITH AN ACCOUNTABILITY PARTNER

"At the beginning of filming I asked all the actors to do an exercise, and it was just standing on your feet for 15 hours," he said. "And as you stand, every hour begin to note where your fatigue is coming in – where do you get stiff, where's painful, when do you have to use the bathroom, when do you get hungry. Write all that down and then work it into the appropriate hour of your shift, and it'll give you the physicality that you need."

Men's Health referred this exercise as NEAT, which stands for non-exercise activity thermogenesis, which takes into account everyday activities which aren't necessarily considered exercise, but get the heart rate up, such as mowing the lawn or vacuuming the floor.

Wyle's workout routine has paid off, as the actor was recently named People's Sexiest Man Alive for 2026.

The news was met with mixed reactions online, with one social media user writing, "Out of all of the people in the world…this is who you pick? You’ve got to be kidding," and another added, "Not even the sexiest in that show."

"More like Noah WHY-le! Ha ha but no seriously who’d you actually pick?" the user joked, while another asked, "is this a joke?"

WATCH HERE: NOAH WYLE IS HAPPY TO BE ABLE TO SUPPORT CEDAR SINAI AT THEIR ANNUAL SUNSET SOIREE EVENT

Others showed their support for the actor, with one commenting, "Thank you for getting it right finally!" and another adding, "#NoahWyle does not just have the looks. He's the whole damn package. That's why he's The Sexiest Man Alive!"

'THE PITT' STAR NOAH WYLE'S 'SEXIEST MAN ALIVE' CROWN SPARKS BACKLASH AS FANS FUME: 'YOU'VE GOT TO BE KIDDING'

The cast of "The Pitt," which also includes Emmy Award winners, Katherine LaNasa and Sean Hatosy, were recently honored by Cedar Sinai Medical Center at the Sunset Soiree, for the series' authentic portrayal of emergency medicine, a moment Wyle called "incredibly gratifying."

"Cedars is like the crown jewel of Los Angeles health care, and being a third generation Angelino, I'm extremely gratified to be recognized by them as an institution," he said. "They were where my first son was born. I've said goodbye to many a friend there. The work that they've given to the people that I've known on both ends of life has been stellar, exemplary, heroic, beautiful. I'm really happy to come out tonight to support them and to try and raise money for them by opening up my rolodex."

Prior to landing the role of Dr. Robbie on "The Pitt," Wyle starred in a different medical drama playing Dr. John Carter in "ER" alongside George Clooney.

He starred on the show for 11 seasons from 1994 to 2005, appearing in over 250 episodes of the show. During an interview with GQ in April, Wyle admitted that despite his success on "ER," he was struggling financially before starring in "The Pitt."

"Well, not to make it a sob story, but everything I pretty much had made and earned on 'ER,' I spent," he told GQ. "I’d taken it down to the studs a couple years ago, to the point where I was doing work for the money, for the experience and for the need to work."

"But I was looking at the rest of my career [thinking], 'Let’s shrink this footprint down and turn it into something that’s sustainable and manageable,'" Wyle added.

item.title: Biological male competing in girls' cross-country race denies another runner and her team a trip to state
item.description: A biological male runner on Camas High's girls' cross-country team displaced a Puyallup girl from state, fueling debate ahead of Initiative 638.
item.content:encoded:
UNIVERSITY PLACE, Wash. — When the Camas High cross-country runner's name was called, Joel Retzlaff yelled, "That's a man!"

Retzlaff is the outspoken father of Skyview High cross-country runner Sierra Retzlaff, who has publicly opposed competing against a biological male. But as Joel made that declaration, nobody walked up to the podium. The Camas boy, who switched to the girls' team midseason, was nowhere to be found.

Camas coach Matt LeGrand — who's in an impossible position — would not comment on why. But there's a decent chance the runner didn't want to face a crowd who knew that, by finishing seventh in regionals, he prevented an actual girl from advancing to state.

DAD BANNED FROM SCHOOL GROUNDS AFTER PROTESTING TRANS RUNNER COMPETING AGAINST HIS DAUGHTER

We won't mention that girl's name here, but she ran for Puyallup High — which finished eighth in the girls' 4A division. The top seven teams go on to state, and if not for the Camas runner's contribution, Puyallup would have advanced.

That team's coach also wouldn’t comment. Understandable. This is the story that, on Halloween, had almost everybody involved spooked.

The key word above is "almost," because there were some people at that meet at Chambers Bay who were willing to speak up. One of them was Carol Brown, a three-time Olympian who won a bronze medal in rowing who can't believe she's on the front lines for an issue she thought was settled a half century ago.

"I fought for Title IX to be allowed to be in sports period, and so I've been fighting this battle. I never thought 50 years later I'd be fighting it again," Brown said. "And I absolutely believe in rights for everyone to participate in sport, but for it to be fair and safe, it has to be based on sex."

What do you think about this Camas runner displacing another girl?

"It's absolutely unfair," Brown said. "The girls put in work, and what I find the hardest to accept is that everyone is saying the girls' voices don't matter, their emotions don't matter, their hard work and once again, like 100 years ago took a second seat to the males."

WASHINGTON GIRLS WALK OFF CROSS COUNTRY MEET IN PROTEST OF MALE ATHLETE, PARENTS REVEAL HOW IT CAME TO THIS

The Camas runner started the season on the boys' team, where he finished 76th in the season's opening JV meet. After switching to the girls' team, he has won a varsity meet and finished second three times. In the past two meets — first at districts last week and again at regionals Saturday — he placed just ahead of Skyview runner Charlie Garrett.

Safe to say Garrett wasn't happy about that.

"I mean, it's really frustrating. I was sad after my race because I was less than a second away [from beating the Camas runner]," said Garrett, admitting that beating him was a side goal of hers Saturday. "But I PR'd, and I qualified for state, so I shouldn't be sad."

What do you think about him not showing up on the podium?

"It shows why he shouldn't be in it," Garrett said. "He has a reason not to show up."

But plenty more opposing the Camas runner's participation showed up Saturday. One of them was Jasmin Faulk, the executive director of Women's Liberation Front (WOLF) — who lost her job at a community college due to a blog post about how "biology still matters." Her emphasis? That fairness in sports shouldn't be a partisan issue.

"The issue is really about the safety and the fairness for women and girls," Faulk said. "That's why we're here, that's why WOLF has chosen to participate and be vocal on this. We have fought for women's rights on all levels and in all areas and sports is just another one that is fairly agreed upon as a general view. This one's an easy one for us to stand by."

I mentioned to her that this doesn’t really feel like a right/left issue — that most Democrats support the separation of biological males and females in sports.

WASHINGTON HIGH SCHOOL GIRL WALKS OFF STARTING LINE ALONE IN PROTEST OF TRANS RUNNER, ENDING HER SEASON

"It's unfortunate, though, because the Democrats are not voicing that. I think that's where the frustration is," Faulk said. "It's a lot easier for the right to take a stand on this one because they've kind of been consistent on this issue for a long time, but the Democrats, I think, have been quieted into it, and the fearmongering in the movement has been the hardest for a lot of people."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The fear is real. Despite this being an 80-20 issue, most people don't want their name attached to their opinions on this matter. One male cross-country runner came over to the crowd wearing XX-XY Athletics gear and said, "I like your shirts" — but said he couldn't accept a "save girls' sports" bracelet or comment on the subject. A female cross-country runner took a picture with that same crowd and said, "You can believe you are something, but you're affecting other people who are actually that and have worked really, really hard for this, and you're taking away a spot from a girl who trained all season." She approached me twice afterward to make sure I wouldn't use her name or school.

But then there are people such as Dawn Land, who held up a sign Saturday reading "Girls deserve fair sports!"

"I think that this boy that is running in the girls' race is grossly unfair. And I'm disgusted at the adults that allowed this to happen," Land said.

Well, Tuesday, adults will have a chance to make sure this doesn't happen in Washington state again. On the ballot is Initiative 638, which would prohibit biological males from competing in girls' K-12 sports.

Carol Brown made a direct plea: "Vote yes if you believe in fair and safe sports for girls."

item.title: Jerry Koosman, hero of the 1969 'Miracle' Mets World Series championship run, dead at 83
item.description: Jerry Koosman won the decisive Game 5 of the 1969 World Series for the Miracle Mets. The left-hander spent 12 of his 19 MLB seasons in Queens.
item.content:encoded:
New York Mets legend Jerry Koosman died Sunday at age 83, the team announced.

Koosman was the winning pitcher in Game 5 of the 1969 World Series, which gave the franchise its first World Series title. That year's squad was dubbed both the "Amazin'" and "Miracle" Mets.

Longtime team employee Jay Horwitz said on social media Koosman had been battling "multiple illnesses."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Mets, whose first season was in 1962, had never been above .500 after just nine games in any of their first seven years in existence. But the Amazin's showed promise early and ran away with the National League East in August.

On Aug. 13 that year, the Mets were 10.0 games behind the Chicago Cubs in the NL East, but in less than a month, they took over first place and wound up running away with the division en route to the title (with the help of the infamous black cat).

PAUL SKENES AND LIVVY DUNNE'S HALLOWEEN COSTUME WILL ENRAGE ANYONE TIRED OF RUSHING THROUGH HOLIDAYS

Koosman pitched to a 2.28 ERA that season, second on the team only to Cy Young Award winner Tom Seaver.

The left-hander spent 12 of his 19 seasons in Queens before spending time with the Minnesota Twins, Chicago White Sox, and Philadelphia Phillies. In New York, he had a 3.09 ERA. He also finished in second place in the 1979 NL Cy Young Award vote, losing to Randy Jones.

His number 36 was retired by the Mets in 2021, becoming the third player in franchise history to have his number retired after Seaver and Mike Piazza. Six others have since followed.

item.title: Holiday airfare hits 10-year high as Thanksgiving and Christmas travel costs soar
item.description: Prices of holiday plane travel are averaging $402 for Thanksgiving and $452 for Christmas as elevated jet fuel costs drive prices to 10-year highs, per Hopper.
item.content:encoded:
Holiday airfares are reaching 10-year highs this year, putting added pressure on Americans planning Thanksgiving and Christmas trips. But a travel expert says there are still ways to save.

Hopper, a travel-booking company, published its 2026 Holiday Travel Index revealing sharp increases in airfare prices compared to last year.

The report analyzed a week's worth of flight searches in September, focusing on lower-priced tickets and accounting for changes in Thanksgiving's date when comparing prices to last year.

POPULAR US AIRPORT CALLED OUT AS 'MOST STRESSFUL' IN AMERICA FOR TRAVELERS

The data shows that domestic round-trip airfare for Thanksgiving is averaging $402, up 31% ($95) from last year. 

International airfare has also increased, particularly for popular destinations in Europe, Mexico and Central America.

For Christmas, domestic round-trip airfare is averaging $452, up 23% ($85) from last year. Flights to Mexico and Central America have increased 23%, while fares to Europe are up 15%.

Hopper attributed the rising price to elevated jet fuel costs.

"Travelers looking ahead to Thanksgiving and Christmas travel will need to plan ahead for a larger travel budget this year, as the 2026 holiday travel is on track to be the most expensive in a decade," the report said.

POPULAR AIRLINE HITS CUSTOMERS WITH STEEP FEE HIKE FOR FIRST TIME IN 8 YEARS

"Months of elevated jet fuel costs due to the conflict in Iran have contributed to Thanksgiving and Christmas airfares reaching 10-year highs."

Gary Leff, a Texas-based aviation expert who founded the blog "View from the Wing," told Fox News Digital that the higher prices will heavily impact families traveling together.

"It's a much bigger deal when you're multiplying increases by, you know, four or more passengers," Leff said.

Leff suggests travelers continue monitoring airfare prices after booking, as they may be able to recover some of the difference if prices fall.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"You buy now and the fare drops, you just have to watch it," he suggested. 

"Don't just buy it and then never look again."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"As long as you're not buying a basic economy ticket, most tickets no longer have change fees," Leff said.

"What that means is that you can call up the airline and apply your old ticket to a new one and generally get a credit back for the difference."

Leff also said common money-saving strategies, such as flying out of a different airport or booking a connecting flight, don't always work.

"If you're looking at an alternate airport that's farther away, there are costs for driving," he said. 

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"You may [have] to park where you otherwise wouldn't, or somebody might drop you off or wouldn't, or the Uber is more expensive."

He said choosing a connecting flight over a nonstop route can introduce additional risks, particularly during the busy holiday season.

"If you take a connection instead of a nonstop, that's more of an opportunity for things to go wrong," Leff said.

He added, "You should always consider your use of miles. If you have them, congratulations, and if you don't, consider accumulating them for the future."

Jessica Mekles of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: DHS official vows to prosecute and deport noncitizens caught illegally voting ahead of midterms
item.description: Department of Homeland Security general counsel James Percival vowed to find, charge and deport noncitizens who cast illegal ballots in midterm elections.
item.content:encoded:
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) general counsel James Percival warned noncitizens against voting illegally during a Saturday appearance on "My View with Lara Trump," saying federal authorities will track them down, charge them and deport them as the country prepares for Tuesday's midterm elections.

"Our message now is, whether it's now or later, if you illegally cast a vote, we will find you, we will charge you, and we will deport you," Percival said.

His comments follow a Wednesday DHS press release announcing that dozens of noncitizens had been arrested on charges related to the agency's nationwide voter fraud crackdown.

"The patriots of ICE have arrested dozens of noncitizens who illegally voted in American elections," Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in the press release. "Some of them have criminal histories that include assault with a dangerous weapon, domestic violence, drug trafficking, burglary, and driving under the influence. The Trump administration will not allow illegal aliens to steal the votes of hardworking American citizens. American elections are for Americans only."

EVERYTHING TO KNOW ABOUT HOUSE ANDSENATE CONTROL, BALLOT MEASURES AND 2026 ELECTION DAY POLL CLOSING

According to DHS, several of those arrested also had criminal records involving offenses ranging from drug crimes to sex offenses.

Meanwhile, the Trump administration's efforts to identify suspected noncitizen voters have faced pushback from some state election officials.

In October, Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs challenged findings from the Justice Department last week after federal officials said investigators had identified more than 400 noncitizens illegally registered to vote in the state, some of whom they said had cast ballots in multiple elections dating back decades.

Hobbs pushed back against the findings, saying the state's review of the list uncovered "several glaring deficiencies."

"This list includes United States citizens and is not reliable. Without individualized proof of ineligibility, it would be both irresponsible and illegal for election officials to decline to process a registered voter’s ballot," he said.

SENATE CONTROL IS A COIN FLIP — AND DEMOCRATS’ PATH RUNS THROUGH TRUMP COUNTRY

"That analysis reflects a significant number of people on your list who are not currently registered to vote or are on inactive status, contradicting your representations that all the individuals included in the list will receive a ballot in this year’s election," he added.

Separately, Percival said more than 200 people have been charged in connection with noncitizen voter fraud.

item.title: Miranda Lambert says fan told her ‘I did shoot him’ after being inspired by ‘Gunpowder & Lead’
item.description: A fan's shocking confession about "Gunpowder & Lead" left Miranda Lambert in tears and forever changed how she viewed the domestic abuse anthem.
item.content:encoded:
Miranda Lambert is reflecting on a fan encounter that left her in tears.

During an appearance on the "And the Writer Is..." podcast, Lambert discussed the powerful impact "Gunpowder & Lead," her 2007 song about a woman confronting an abusive partner after he is released from jail, has had on her fans.

"It's such a huge staple for me in my catalog, just the subject matter, and how I got to that and who I got to write it with, and the stories I’ve heard from women over the years who have come up to me and said, ‘That song saved my life,’" Lambert said of the hit, which was released on her album "Crazy Ex-Girlfriend" and was co-written with Heather Little."At some meet-and-greets, I've heard some crazy things."

She recalled one woman who approached her in Indianapolis and said she didn’t want a photo.

"She's like, ‘I just want to tell you that I finally had enough, and that song gave me the courage, and I did shoot him — and I got off,’" Lambert said.

"I was like, ‘OK,’" she continued. "She was dead serious. She was hardcore. And then we cried together."

Lambert said the woman’s story left her overwhelmed.

"When someone tells you something like that about something you wrote that didn’t actually happen to you, it’s very intense," she said. "She was like third in line at the meet-and-greet, and I had like 85 people, and I was like, ‘I’m going to need a minute.’ I needed to take a breath, hug her and recover from what that is."

The moment changed Lambert’s perspective on the song.

item.title: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson injured once again and out of the game after only one play against Bills
item.description: Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb on his very first snap against the Buffalo Bills after missing three straight games with an ankle sprain.
item.content:encoded:
Lamar Jackson's return to the Baltimore Ravens offense lasted all of one play on Sunday before he was injured once again.

The Baltimore Ravens quarterback started his first game since Oct. 4 against the Buffalo Bills. However, on his first play in nearly a month and on the Ravens' first offensive snap of the game, Jackson injured his right thumb.

Jackson hit his thumb against Buffalo defensive end Greg Rousseau's arm as he threw the football. He immediately grabbed the thumb in obvious pain.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Jackson was taken to the Ravens' medical tent and then immediately escorted to the team's locker room while wearing a towel around his entire right hand.

The team initially reported Jackson was questionable to return with a right thumb injury, but within a few minutes, it said Jackson was done for the game.

The quick change in status suggests the Ravens are dealing with a dislocated or fractured thumb.

It is impossible for a quarterback with an injured thumb on his throwing hand to spin the football.

Tyler Huntley took over at quarterback for the Ravens.

And this is all too familiar for Baltimore. But it would soon get worse.

Huntley left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury. He was questionable to return.

Third-string emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano, who had never played in a regular-season game, was thrust into duty while Huntley sat on the bench.

Rough day for Baltimore.

Jackson has played four games for the Ravens this season and has been highly productive, completing 68 of 96 passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while adding 144 rushing yards and a touchdown.

The Ravens were 3-1 in his starts before Sunday.

But Jackson suffered a high-ankle sprain in the Oct. 4 victory over Tennessee and has missed the past three games, with his mobility and ability to tolerate the pain remaining the primary concerns.

If the Ravens' worst fears about a dislocation or fracture become the situation they must navigate, Jackson will probably miss more than just the remainder of this game.

item.description: Heidi Klum's gruesome severed-hand costume stole the show, but Zendaya's Halle Berry tribute and Lisa Rinna's Kylie Jenner look turned heads too.
item.content:encoded:
From a bloody, severed hand to iconic recreations and impersonations, Hollywood's finest showed up for Halloween this year.

Here are some of the best looks.

Heidi Klum once again cemented her status as the queen of Halloween with a gruesome transformation. The supermodel dressed as a giant severed version of her own left hand for her annual Halloween party in New York City.

HEIDI KLUM UNRECOGNIZABLE IN DRAMATIC COACHELLA DISGUISE AS 'TECHNO HEXEN'

The elaborate costume featured long red nails, her thumb ring, wedding band and even a tattoo of husband Tom Kaulitz’s name. Klum said the look took about six hours to put on, while the prosthetics and costume were developed over several months. Her face appeared through the center of the hand, with blood dripping from her mouth and fake tendons hanging from the wrist.

Zendaya paid tribute to Halle Berry by recreating the actress’ iconic 2000 "X-Men" premiere look. With help from stylist Law Roach, Zendaya wore the same butter-yellow, brown and white Lanvin string bikini top and matching low-rise, wide-leg pants Berry wore to the film’s New York premiere.

HEIDI KLUM LEADS CELEBS WITH OVER-THE-TOP COUPLES' HALLOWEEN COSTUMES THROUGH THE YEARS

She completed the fashion homage with pointed-toe heels, tinted sunglasses and Berry-inspired short hair.

Lisa Rinna transformed into Kylie Jenner for Halloween, recreating Jenner’s memorable orange look from the "Marty Supreme" premiere.

Rinna wore a skin-tight orange dress with hip cutouts, bright orange heels, a long dark wig, smoky eye makeup and a chunky silver cross necklace.

"King Lisa," Rinna captioned the photos, referencing Jenner’s former "King Kylie" era. Jenner appeared to approve of the impersonation, commenting, "Thought this was me." NBC New York reported.

Dylan Sprouse and his wife, model Barbara Palvin, embraced a "Nightmare Before Christmas" theme for their Halloween celebration. Palvin underwent a dramatic transformation into Oogie Boogie, complete with green makeup, a burlap-style hat, a zigzag costume and matching green boots.

Sprouse complemented his wife’s elaborate look with a black pinstriped suit and oversized bow tie. The couple hosted their first official Sprouse House Halloween party in Los Angeles.

Rita Ora paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton by dressing as the country music icon for a Halloween party in New York City. Ora channeled Parton’s signature blonde hair and glamorous country style with a blue button-down shirt, visible push-up bra, jeans, a studded red belt and red Gucci heels.

DOLLY PARTON'S PATH FROM NASHVILLE NEWCOMER TO BILLBOARD'S NO. 1 COUNTRY MUSIC ARTIST OF ALL TIME

Ora’s costume came as several celebrities honored Parton this Halloween following the singer’s death in August.

Ashley Graham transformed into Ariel from Disney’s "The Little Mermaid." The model lip-synced to "Part of Your World" in a video posted on Instagram, while showing off her mermaid-inspired costume and glamorous red-haired look.

Bethenny Frankel dressed up as Tinker Bell for Halloween, showing off a bright green mini dress and fairy-inspired look. The former "Real Housewives of New York City" star completed the costume with wings and matching pixie-dust flair while sharing videos of the transformation on social media.

"Faith, trust and a little pixie dust," Frankel captioned one of her Halloween posts. In another video, she referenced the Peter Pan character with the message, "Nobody is clipping my wings."

item.title: Women's sex drive treatment linked to higher rates of heart attack and stroke
item.description: A study of 6,000+ postmenopausal women links testosterone therapy to higher rates of heart attack, stroke and heart failure in new research.
item.content:encoded:
Postmenopausal women who use testosterone therapy could face a higher risk of heart attack, stroke and other cardiovascular problems, new research suggests.

The research, presented at the 2026 annual meeting of The Menopause Society last month in San Diego, looked at more than 6,000 postmenopausal women age 45 and older, comparing those who received testosterone therapy with those who did not. Women with a history of cardiovascular disease were excluded.

Among women receiving testosterone, 3.8% experienced a first-time cardiovascular event compared with 0.5% of women who were not receiving the treatment, according to The Menopause Society.

POPULAR ARTIFICIAL SWEETENER LINKED TO POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS HEART RISK

Those events included heart attack, stroke, heart failure and other cardiovascular problems.

Testosterone is a sex hormone produced by the ovaries and adrenal glands that plays a role in sexual desire, as well as muscle and bone health, mood and cognition, according to Cleveland Clinic.

Anna Cabeca, a Dallas-based board-certified OB-GYN and menopause expert, told Fox News Digital that the differences between the two groups — women who received testosterone and those who did not — deserve attention.

"The difference between 3.8% and 0.5% is certainly significant enough to warrant attention, but we need to be careful about what these numbers actually tell us," said Cabeca, who was not involved in the study.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

That amounts to about 38 cardiovascular events per 1,000 women receiving testosterone compared with five per 1,000 women who were not, the doctor noted.

For women considering testosterone therapy, Cabeca said doctors should look at the patient's overall health, including heart history, blood pressure, cholesterol, metabolic health, medications and family history.

"Sexual health is an essential part of overall health, and women deserve to have their concerns about libido, arousal and intimacy taken seriously, particularly during and after menopause," she added.

While testosterone can improve sexual desire and satisfaction in appropriately selected postmenopausal women, the possible benefits should be weighed against potential risks, Cabeca advised.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

In cases when testosterone is appropriate, she favors careful dosing, monitoring and regular checks of a patient's symptoms and lab results.

There are important limitations to the new findings, the researchers acknowledged.

The study was observational, meaning the researchers looked at outcomes among women who were already receiving testosterone rather than assigning the treatment in a controlled trial.

As a result, the study can show a link between testosterone use and cardiovascular events, but cannot prove that the treatment caused them.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Women who received testosterone may also have differed from those who did not in ways that affected their heart risk, including age, blood pressure, diabetes, cholesterol levels or other health factors, Cabeca said.

"This is an important safety signal that deserves further investigation, not definitive evidence of causation," she added.

Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.

Deirdre Bardolf of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: Connecticut Dem Sen Chris Murphy hospitalized Saturday for stroke
item.description: Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., was rushed to Johns Hopkins after suffering a stroke Saturday while attending his son's hockey game, his chief of staff says.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., was hospitalized after experiencing a stroke, his chief of staff Allison Herwitt said in a statement released Sunday.

Murphy, who is not running in the midterms but has been stumping for Democrats, began feeling numbness in his arm Saturday afternoon while at his son’s hockey game and was taken to a local hospital before being transferred to Johns Hopkins for further monitoring, according to Allison Herwitt.

WHAT TO DO IF SOMEONE IS HAVING A STROKE, AFTER JILL BIDEN REVEALED DEBATE-NIGHT FEARS

"He was taken to a local hospital, where it was discovered he had experienced a stroke. He was transferred to Johns Hopkins for further monitoring and is responding well to treatment," she said in a statement.

"The doctors are encouraged by his progress, he is awake and alert, and we are optimistic he will make a full recovery."

Murphy was first elected to the Senate in 2013 and has been viewed as a potential 2028 Democratic presidential primary candidate. 

He has spent the past several weeks on the campaign trail with Democrats as he stumped to help retake control of the Senate majority in the midterm elections. He had been scheduled to campaign for Democrats in New Hampshire on Sunday.

Murphy is 53 years old, born August 3, 1973.

item.title: Panera Bread grabs top honors for America's highest-rated fast-food breakfast item
item.description: An avocado, egg white, tomato and spinach sandwich topped a Consumer Reports fast-food breakfast ranking, as Panera Bread beat out McDonald's and Starbucks.
item.content:encoded:
A popular restaurant chain grabbed four of the top 10 spots in a recent Consumer Reports fast-food breakfast item ranking — with its avocado, egg white and spinach sandwich winning first place and edging out items from major chains like McDonald’s and Starbucks.

Panera Bread's avocado, egg white and spinach sandwich is served on a sprouted grain bagel flat and costs $5.

Containing egg whites, tomato slices, spinach, aged white cheddar cheese and avocado, the sandwich clocks in at 410 calories and 21 grams of protein, according to Consumer Reports.

SOUTHERN BREAKFAST CHAIN IN JUST 3 STATES BEATS MCDONALD'S, CHICK-FIL-A FOR BEST IN AMERICA

The organization gave the sandwich an overall score of 75, a four out of five nutrition score and a five out of five sensory score, which is based on flavor and texture attributes.

Fox News Digital reached out to Panera Bread, headquartered in Fenton, Missouri, for comment. 

While McDonald’s made the list, other fast-food empires like Wendy’s and Burger King were left behind.

McDonald’s Egg White Delight earned the 13th spot in the ranking with an overall score of 66, while its Egg McMuffin was ranked 19th with a score of 64.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Two other Panera items won second and third place in the ranking: a steel-cut oatmeal with strawberries and pecans, and another oatmeal with almonds, quinoa and honey.

Other chains such as Jamba Juice and Au Bon Pain were represented on the list, with Jamba Juice’s oatmeal with strawberries and brown sugar crumble earning fourth place.

Dunkin' earned spots in the ranking as well, with items including the whole grain oatmeal with dried fruit and the veggie egg white on an English muffin.

Panera’s Greek yogurt with mixed berries was also listed, and the chain’s ham, egg and cheese on whole-grain bread was one spot ahead of the McDonald’s Egg McMuffin.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

A few Starbucks menu items made the cut as well, such as the red pepper sous vide egg white bites, the spinach, feta and egg white wrap and a berry yogurt parfait.

Panera customers on Reddit were somewhat divided in their opinions about the spinach, avocado and egg white sandwich.

One criticism that surfaced was the amount of avocado. 

"It had to have been less than 1/8th of an avocado," a Reddit user said in a thread about Panera Bread. "When I say I got one chunk, it was literally like one slice that you can see in the advertisement pic."

Another person claimed to have been ordering the sandwich for a while, but felt it’s not quite what it used to be.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I've been a loyal fan of this breakfast sandwich and have probably ordered it at least 50 times now, as a ‘treat’ for breakfast. I've seen a steady decrease in quality, and the last time I ordered it the bread was so thin and sad," the person wrote.

"Ah, yes, my favorite breakfast sandwich," said a fan of the menu item. 

"I hope they never get rid of this," said another individual.

Other people on social media shared a variety of different opinions.

"I'm happy with just a Sausage McMuffin," wrote one man on Facebook.

"For me personally, the best breakfast sandwich is the McDonald's Sausage Biscuit, then after that would be the Chic-fil-A Chicken Biscuit!" said another person.

item.title: Will Democrats block the stock trading ban again after the midterm elections?
item.description: Senate Democrats voted against a bill that would have banned Congress stock trading. A new poll shows political corruption is voters' top concern.
item.content:encoded:
Americans do not agree on much these days, but they certainly agree on this: Members of Congress should not get rich trading stocks while writing the very laws that move those stocks.

The failure to ban insider trading in Congress is part of a broader rot now engulfing the swamp. Political corruption, in general, has become a top concern for voters — and for good reason. A new CNBC poll shows, perhaps surprisingly, that it is the most important issue facing the nation: According to CNBC, 36% of voters ranked corruption as the top issue facing the country. To these voters, corruption, and corrupt acts like insider trading, are even more important than the cost of groceries and gas.

Despite a slew of arrests in Minnesota, California and New York, where well-connected liberal groups and activists were caught stealing billions in taxpayer dollars, Democrats hold a four-point edge, 35% to 31%, on which party would better handle political corruption. Of those surveyed by CNBC, 93% said members of Congress and the president should not own or trade stock in companies that hold federal contracts, and 89% said companies owned by a sitting president’s immediate family should not receive federal contracts at all.

DOZENS OF HOUSE DEMOCRATS REJECT BILL FUSING CONGRESSIONAL STOCK BAN WITH FEDERAL VOTER ID

That all seems reasonable enough.

But apparently, it isn’t reasonable for Democrats. On Sept. 30, Senate Democrats rejected the Stop Insider Trading Act after it had already passed the House with Democratic votes. If it had passed, the law would have barred members of Congress, their spouses and their dependent children from buying new stock in public companies while in office. It would have also forced public notice before lawmakers could sell what they already hold.

CARVILLE TELLS DEMOCRATS TO 'JUST QUIT FIGHTING' AGAINST VOTER ID REQUIREMENTS, WARNS IT POLLS AT 75%

But every single Democrat in the Senate voted no.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s, D-N.Y., excuse? He claimed Republicans set the bill up to fail, loading it with intentional "poison pills" so that it would never pass. He also called it toothless, and said it didn’t go far enough. Democrats pointed to a provision requiring voters to show identification at the polls, which an overwhelming majority of Americans support and virtually every other first-world country requires.

DEMS HAND GOP FRESH MIDTERM WEAPON BY OPPOSING WIDELY USED VOTER ID

Schumer’s other objection — that the bill doesn’t go far enough — is hard to square with his record. One does not refuse to lock his front door because he would prefer an elaborate home security system. A partial reform on the books beats a perfect one that lives only in tailored press releases. Even more to the point: Democrats ran the Senate for years and never delivered the "real" ban on insider trading they now disingenuously purport to want.

Senate Democrats’ recent vote against the Stop Insider Trading Act also puts attention back on Nancy Pelosi’s household, which sold 2,000 shares of Visa, worth between $500,000 and $1 million, on July 1, 2024. Less than three months later, the Biden Justice Department filed an antitrust lawsuit against Visa. The stock promptly dropped.

As attorney and longtime Trump advisor Michael Caputo recently put it, "Plenty of legal analysts have questioned the suit... whatever the lawsuit ultimately accomplishes, its most conspicuous result so far has been helping a well-connected investor avoid the losses other Visa shareholders suffered."

That well-connected investor, of course, is "Princess Nancy" herself.

However, the Visa sale wasn’t the first time hubby Paul Pelosi’s stock trading timing attracted scrutiny. In 2022, he bought more than $1 million in Nvidia call options weeks before Congress voted on major subsidies for the chip industry. He then sold them once the story broke.

What funny timing!

The more things change, the more they stay the same. At the turn of the 20th century, this was sometimes referred to in the jargon of the day as "honest graft." In New York, insiders like George Washington Plunkitt, who ran New York’s infamous political machine of Tammany Hall, declared, "There's an honest graft, and I'm an example of how it works. I might sum up the whole thing by saying: ‘I’ve seen my opportunities and I took ‘em.’"

Today, Pelosi’s corruption is so obvious that stock-trading platforms like PelosiTracker, Quiver Quantitative and Unusual Whales attempt to mimic her stock portfolio. In 2024, that portfolio returned more than double the S&P 500.

EX-HOUSE DEM WHO RIPPED CONGRESSIONAL STOCK TRADING BAN AS 'BULLS---' CHANGES HER TUNE IN COMEBACK BID

The American people are not asking for much. They want the people who write the rules to stop playing the very game those rules govern. Republicans put a bill on the floor that would do that. Senate Democrats killed it.

The Senate is out until after the election. When Congress returns for the lame-duck session, it should take the bill up again before the end of the year. Senate Democrats can redeem themselves then — at least on this score.

item.title: Buffalo Bills defense is 'horrible' and that means team cannot win the Super Bowl, Terry Bradshaw says on Fox
item.description: Terry Bradshaw declared the Buffalo Bills won't win the Super Bowl, calling their defense "horrible" ahead of the big Baltimore Ravens matchup.
item.content:encoded:
Terry Bradshaw was known as the Blonde Bomber during his playing days when he helped the Pittsburgh Steelers win four Super Bowls, and he kind of lived up to that nickname during the opening segment of the Fox NFL Sunday show by dropping a truth bomb on the Buffalo Bills.

The FOX studio crew was discussing the day's upcoming games and Bradshaw discussed the AFC showcase matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens.

"This is gonna be a fun game to watch," Bradshaw began harmlessly enough. "Last year, they played each other and the final score was 41-40, Buffalo. You got two great quarterbacks, all right?"

Yes, all right.

"Now you got [James] Cook, and then you got the great running back for the Baltimore Ravens, [Derrick] Henry. So you got great running backs, great quarterbacks, but here's the deal, no good defense," Bradshaw said.

Here we go.

"Buffalo's defense is horrible," Bradshaw then added looking into the camera. "And with [Lamar] Jackson back, I expect him to throw the football, play action, even though Lamar has a bad ankle. This game's gonna be fun to watch it.

LAMAR JACKSON HITS BACK AT CRITICS WITH FAITHFUL MESSAGE ON SOCIAL MEDIA

"And if there's one thing I've learned from the NFL this season, if you don't have a great defense ... you're not going to win a Super Bowl. You may have a great offense, but you will not win a Super Bowl.

"Buffalo right now, fun to watch. Fun to watch. But they're not gonna win a Super Bowl."

Well, so three things could be happening next:

Firstly, Bills Mafia might be coming for Bradshaw. That is a practical certainty and the argument will center around the Bills being able to address their No. 30th ranked scoring defense or the offense being able to overcome that subpar defense.

Secondly, the Bills prove Bradshaw wrong on Feb. 14 when Super Bowl LXI is played.

Thirdly, Bradshaw is proven absolutely correct.

SUPER BOWL LXI GETS PAT MCAFEE TREATMENT AS ESPN ADDS ALTERNATE BROADCAST

History is on Bradshaw's side.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

No NFL team has has ever won a Super Bowl despite ranking in the bottom three in the regular-season in points allowed.

2026 NFL SEASON PREDICTIONS: DIVISION WINNERS, PLAYOFF TEAMS AND SUPER BOWL PICK REVEALED

The worst scoring defense to win a Super Bowl was the 2011 New York Giants, who ranked 25th in points allowed, giving up 25 points per game. The next-worst were the 2006 Indianapolis Colts, ranked 23rd, and the 2009 New Orleans Saints, ranked 20th.

The Bills, under first-year head coach Joe Brady, have shown improvement on offense from a year ago, which is logical since Brady is an offense-minded coach.

Conversely, losing Sean McDermott, who was a defense-minded coach, has apparently hurt the team on that side of the ball.

item.title: Shootings near 5 college communities leave 3 dead, at least 29 injured
item.description: A violent Halloween across the U.S. leaves police investigating five shootings near college campuses in Indiana, Delaware, Alabama, Illinois and Colorado, while Dallas shootings leave four dead.
item.content:encoded:
Shootings in four college communities over the weekend left three people dead and at least 29 others injured.

Indiana, Delaware, Alabama, Illinois and Colorado police are each investigating shootings in crowded parties near college communities, according to police and university statements.

Seven were hospitalized in Bloomington, Indiana, near Indiana University's homecoming, while the University of Delaware is still counting victims (six are reportedly hospitalized) and the Magic City Classic football game between Alabama A&M and Alabama State near Legion Field in Birmingham, Alabama, left at least one dead and eight wounded. 

In Bloomington, Illinois, eight people were shot near Illinois Wesleyan University, leaving a 19-year-old woman dead. A shooting in Boulder, Colorado, left one University of Colorado Boulder student dead and another critically injured.

SHOOTING AFTER MAGIC CITY CLASSIC IN ALABAMA LEAVES 1 DEAD, 8 INJURED

After midnight near Indiana University, officers monitoring a large crowd around Kirkwood Avenue and Dunn Street heard shots around 1:30 a.m. ET and saw a man with a firearm running from the area, Bloomington police said.

Officers took the man into custody near Dunn Meadow, and recovered a gun and shell casings in the area. Police said it remains unclear whether the suspect fired any shots.

No deaths were reported in Bloomington, and police said they did not know whether there were additional victims.

FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY SHOOTING LEAVES 12 INJURED, INCLUDING 6 CHILDREN, NEAR FOOTBALL STADIUM

A disturbance in the crowd may have preceded the shooting, police said. Indiana University police and Indiana State Police assisted in the response.

In Newark, Delaware, a shooting on Saturday night rocked the University of Delaware.

"We are deeply concerned about the shooting on Main Street Saturday night, which has impacted our entire community," the school's director of media relations Peter Bothum told Fox News Digital in a statement. "We are grateful to the Newark Police Department, which is leading the investigation. We will continue to communicate confirmed information, which will be shared on a dedicated alerts page (udel.edu/about/alerts) and updated as we learn more."

University President Laura Carlson said victims were receiving care and thanked Newark police, campus police and other first responders for providing on-scene care.

POLICE OFFICER, WOMAN SHOT NEAR NOTRE DAME AFTER FOOTBALL TAILGATES

"I am writing to you about the shooting last night in Newark on Main Street, although it is difficult to know what to say when violence like this erupts in our community," she wrote in an email to the school community.

"We are all impacted," she continued. "I ask that you keep the victims in your thoughts and hearts as they receive care. Please also recognize the impact and toll on our students and community members who were on Main Street last night and witnessed this violence."

The university did not provide a confirmed number of victims or say whether anyone had died, but a report indicated at least six were hospitalized. The investigation is being led by Newark police. The school urged students and staff to follow its campus alerts page for confirmed updates.

In Birmingham, Alabama, one person was killed and eight others were wounded Saturday night after the Magic City Classic football game near Legion Field, police said. Officers found nine people with gunshot wounds in the 400 block of Graymont Avenue West shortly after 7:50 p.m. ET.

SEVERAL UNIVERSITY OF IOWA STUDENTS WOUNDED IN DOWNTOWN SHOOTING AFTER FIGHT ERUPTS NEAR CAMPUS

One victim was in critical condition and seven others were stable, authorities said.

Michael Pickett, chief of the Birmingham Police Department, said most spectators and families had left the stadium property after the game, but the shooting happened nearby, where vendors were set up along Graymont Avenue.

He said he was "very grateful that more people weren’t injured."

Police spokesperson De'Rell Freeman said one person had been detained and transported to police headquarters for questioning, and "multiple weapons" had been found and secured.

Alabama State and Alabama A&M are historically Black universities and archrivals whose annual contest has been played for more than 100 years. Nearly 70,000 fans attended Saturday's game, won by Alabama A&M 31-28. The event draws some of the largest crowds in the country for games played in their college football division.

The Magic City Classic has such a deep history that Alabama State coach Eddie Robinson Jr., a former NFL linebacker and alumnus of the school, proposed creating a Hall of Fame for the game.

POLICE MAKE ARREST AFTER GUNFIRE DURING CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME LEAVES 1 DEAD

In Bloomington, Illinois, police responded just before 1:25 a.m. Sunday to a shooting near Illinois Wesleyan University and found multiple people at the scene with gunshot wounds.

Officers immediately secured the scene with assistance from the Illinois State Police and McLean County Sheriff's Office, and seven victims were taken to the hospital for treatment. A 19-year-old woman was pronounced dead at the scene by the McLean County Coroner's Office and another woman remains in critical condition.

ATF Chicago confirmed Sunday afternoon that it is assisting with the investigation.

SEARCH UNDERWAY FOR SUSPECTED GUNMAN OUTSIDE NOTRE DAME FOOTBALL GAME VS MICHIGAN STATE

In Boulder, Colorado, an overnight shooting on University Hill killed one University of Colorado Boulder student and left another critically injured.

Just before 11:30 p.m. Saturday, Boulder police officers responded to a home for a reported shooting. Officers arrived at the scene in less than two minutes and found two 19-year-old men with gunshot wounds. Both were taken to the hospital where one was pronounced dead. The second victim remains in critical condition.

Both victims were University of Colorado Boulder students, and the Boulder County Coroner's Office will release the identity of the victim who died, according to a news release from the city of Boulder.

Officials said the shooting report was the second call to the home Saturday night. Earlier Saturday night, Boulder police responded to a noise complaint involving a large party at the home. Officers contacted the people who lived at the home and cited them for having a nuisance party. Following police intervention, the party ended, and hundreds of attendees left the area. A smaller group remained inside the home.

Detectives said they believe a group of people later attempted to force their way into the house. Shortly after that scuffle, shots were fired inside the home, striking the two victims.

Detectives have interviewed roughly 20 witnesses and continue to pursue numerous leads, according to the city.

Detectives released photos of two persons of interest and other possible witnesses. The first person of interest was described as a man with short, dark hair and facial hair, wearing a red hooded sweatshirt underneath a black jacket. The second person of interest was described as a man with short, dark hair, wearing a black shirt with Art the Clown on it and a silver chain necklace.

"My heart breaks for the victims and for everyone impacted by this senseless violence. Our community deserves to feel safe, and we will not accept this kind of violence in Boulder," Boulder Police Chief Steve Redfearn wrote in a statement. "I want to assure these families and our community that we are doing everything in our power to find those responsible and hold them accountable."

In addition to the shootings near campuses, police in Dallas say four people are dead and 15 are injured following three separate shootings in a Dallas neighborhood. Police Chief Daniel Comeaux said police are still trying to determine if the shootings were related or what led to them. Comeaux said some arrests were made, but he did not specify how many or what charges were involved.

"This is a really big scene. It's spread out," Comeaux said. "We are interviewing some individuals right now that we have arrested, still trying to figure out exactly how it ties into all the shootings out here."

In Fayetteville, Arkansas, six people were taken to hospitals with gunshot wounds from a shooting that happened early Sunday. No arrests have been made, police said in a news release. A preliminary investigation indicates an altercation preceded the shooting.

Fox News' Bradford Betz and Angelica Stabile and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: 'Squad' rakes in record $2.35M while slamming the door on cop donations
item.description: The Squad Victory Fund raised a record $2.35 million this cycle while explicitly barring donations from the Fraternal Order of Police union.
item.content:encoded:
Hey cops, your money's no good here.

A joint fundraising committee for four progressive House Democrats has raised a record $2.35 million so far this election cycle, while barring donations from the Fraternal Order of Police, according to federal filings and the committee’s disclosure.

The Squad Victory Fund is authorized by Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.; Ilhan Omar, D-Minn.; Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass.; and Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich. The fundraising gives the four lawmakers and their allied political groups a shared vehicle to collect and distribute campaign contributions.

ILHAN OMAR’S WEALTH SCANDAL TAKES A TURN JUST ONE DAY AFTER RAID OF HER DC HOME

The fund’s donor rules also make clear which groups it says it will not accept money from, and one is the Fraternal Order of Police, the nation’s largest police organization. It also bars donations from corporations, federal lobbyists and fossil fuel interests. The disclosure does not explain the FOP exclusion.

SOCIALIST PRIMARY SWEEP SPARKS LAUNCH OF NEW RESOURCE LAYING OUT WHAT’S AT STAKE IN 2026

The fund’s other participants include four allied PACs. Contributions are generally divided equally among the eight participants, with each slated to receive 12.5%, though donors may designate their contributions for a specific participant.

The fund has raised $2,351,388.02 in the 2025–2026 election cycle, its highest total to date, according to its FEC summary.

Through March 31, 2026, it had spent about $1.6 million and reported roughly $68,000 in cash on hand. The committee remains active, so those figures may change.

Contributions are not tax-deductible, the disclosure notes.

item.title: Texas firefighters rescue distressed raccoon after its head gets stuck in a hole in a tree
item.description: Video shows Austin firefighters using a catch pole to free a raccoon stuck in a tree hollow, but the animal's limp body raised immediate concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Raccoons are known for getting into all kinds of things while out scavenging for food. They will tip over garbage cans, rip open bags and even climb into an attic looking for food if they can find a way in.

They will also use tree hollows for dens. Assuming, of course, that they fit into said tree hollow — which isn’t always the case, as firefighters in Austin, Texas, found out last week when a raccoon got its head stuck in a hole in a tree.

A concerned neighbor called the Austin Fire Department to see if they could help the trash panda out. It wasn’t reported if the raccoon was after food or if it was in the market for a den when it became stuck in the tree.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

What was reported is that the firefighters answered the call, used a Jaws of Life-type tool, and freed the stuck animal from the hole in the tree.

The raccoon’s apparent limpness as it was lowered to the ground caused concern that its scavenging days were behind it. The firefighters addressed those concerns.

"RACCOON RESCUE UPDATE: HE’S OKAY! For everyone who has been concerned about the raccoon Austin firefighters recently rescued from a tree, we have good news!" the Austin Firefighter Association wrote.

"Although the video may make it look like the raccoon is unconscious or has passed away when crews free him and lower him to the ground using a tool called a catch pole, we’re happy to report that he was alive and unharmed!"

TAXIDERMIED RACCOONS ARE SEEING UNPRECEDENTED DEMAND THANKS TO NORWEGIAN SOCCER STAR ERLING HAALAND

Perhaps the raccoon was simply embarrassed by the miscalculation of the size of its head in relation to the size of the hole. I'm sure it's not the first nor will it be the last raccoon to do so.

"After what we can only imagine was a long, stressful struggle with his head stuck in the tree, our little friend was understandably tired. But when firefighters handed him over to Animal Control, he was okay!," the update continued.

"Thank you to everyone who reached out and showed concern for this little guy. We’re glad this rescue had a happy ending!"

What more can you ask for from a raccoon with its head stuck in a tree hollow story than a happy ending?

item.title: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers at Detroit church
item.description: Haley Stevens stood next to Mike Rogers at a Detroit church after Abdul El-Sayed's campaign withdrew her invitation over the antisemitic ad dispute.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., endorsed Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday amid Democratic infighting that has roiled the Michigan Senate race.

The endorsement came on the heels of Stevens' appearance alongside Rogers at Detroit’s Perfecting Church, where Fox News confirmed she attended a service. Stevens lost in the primary to fellow Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, and has been critical of his unwillingness to condemn the overt antisemitism of some of his supporters. 

"Hey Michigan, as you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul [El-Sayed] said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away and he's right. And that's why I'm endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today," Stevens said in a video posted on X.

Stevens said she remains "a very proud Democrat" who loves Michigan but could not support El-Sayed, citing his backing from political streamer Hasan Piker.

"I'm honored to have Haley Stevens support today. I'm honored to have earned that vote," Rogers told reporters gathered outside the church. "This is more a statement about standing together against hate and the future of this state and this country than it is anything else," he added.

The appearance came after Stevens was disinvited from a planned church event with El-Sayed, the man who narrowly defeated her in Michigan’s August Democratic primary.

The reversal left Stevens at the same church as Rogers, El-Sayed’s Republican opponent.

HALEY STEVENS RIPPED BY FELLOW DEMS FOR REFUSING TO EXPLICITLY BACK EL-SAYED: 'STAY THE F--- OFF TELEVISION'

Stevens has pressed El-Sayed to condemn an outside group’s ad linking U.S. support for Israel to higher grocery prices, which she called antisemitic.

El-Sayed said the ad was not produced by his campaign and that he disagreed with its contents.

Rep. Debbie Dingell, D-Mich., who helped organize the planned appearance, said Stevens was asked to skip it after the dispute became a distraction and upset the church’s bishop.

FORMER RIVAL DODGES FULL-THROATED EL-SAYED ENDORSEMENT AFTER BITTER SENATE PRIMARY

El-Sayed’s campaign also asked Stevens to stay away from its remaining events.

Stevens fiancé, Jason Turkish, has previously endorsed Rogers and appeared at a Rogers campaign event, saying he could not support El-Sayed because of his positions on Israel.

The dispute has put a spotlight on Democratic divisions in a close Senate race that could help determine control of the chamber.

item.title: ‘Back to the Future’ star Christopher Lloyd confesses he was ‘hooked’ on cocaine during ‘Taxi’ years
item.description: Christopher Lloyd reveals in his memoir how cocaine and alcohol became "entrenched" in his life, leading to a dramatic rehab escape in Arizona.
item.content:encoded:
Christopher Lloyd is opening up about his decades-long struggle with alcohol and drug addiction, revealing how substance abuse became "entrenched" in his life before he ultimately sought treatment and found sobriety.

The 88-year-old actor detailed his battle in his new memoir, "In My Own Time," and discussed his recovery during a recent interview with his "Back to the Future" co-star, Michael J. Fox.

In the book, Lloyd recalled that his cocaine abuse began after a woman approached him at a Los Angeles nightclub and asked if he wanted to "do a snort."

BRAT PACK ICON ANDREW MCCARTHY SAYS DRINKING 'DERAILED MY CAREER ENTIRELY'

"She meant cocaine, which at that point I had never tried," Lloyd wrote. "I hadn’t been out looking for it, but I said all right. We went out to her car and did a couple of lines. That was all it took. I was hooked almost immediately. I loved it, and that was where my cocaine abuse began."

"Within a couple of years of my arrival in Los Angeles, cocaine, alcohol, and pot had become woven into my life in a serious way," he continued. "It wasn’t just the occasional weekend indulgence. It got entrenched."

'CADDYSHACK' STAR MICHAEL O'KEEFE CLAIMS COCAINE WAS BUDGETED ON SET, ADMITS FILMING SCENES HIGH

Lloyd explained that he made a point of staying sober while working, but his substance use intensified once filming ended.

"I never went onstage or in front of a camera high or drunk, because I knew I would lose control of myself," he wrote. "But once the curtain came down or the director said, ‘That’s a wrap,’ all bets were off."

"I just knew I liked it, and before long it had a hold on me," he added.

Another substance that had a hold on him was alcohol.

ZACH BRYAN ADMITS HE DRANK '15 BEERS A DAY' AS PART OF 'PERFECT ROUTINE' BEFORE QUITTING ALCOHOL

Lloyd recalled being confronted about his drinking during a routine medical appointment. When a nurse asked how many drinks he had each day, he answered, "Two or three."

"She said, ‘You’re an alcoholic,’" Lloyd wrote. "It stunned me, because I didn’t think what I was doing was a problem."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

But he quickly noticed that his substance abuse eventually began affecting his life on screen and off.

"I was recognizing that I had a problem, and if I couldn’t yet appreciate that I was putting my life at stake, I could at least see that it was endangering my career," he wrote. "I had gotten into these things pretty seriously and I needed help to get under control and get out of it."

"At some point, it became clear that I needed treatment," Lloyd continued.

In 1993, Lloyd’s psychologist arranged for him to enter treatment in Arizona. He recalled being "completely wasted" when he boarded a plane to a treatment facility, where he refused to stay and ran into a barbed-wire fence after leaving. 

"I refused to stay," he wrote. "I bolted out of the place and, drunk and disoriented, ran straight into a barbed-wire fence that tore up my face and left me a bloody mess."

He was eventually admitted to Sierra Tucson, where he remained for five weeks.
