"That was the beginning, but not the end of it," Lloyd wrote. "I relapsed a few times after that."

Lloyd said he continued attending a private 12-step meeting for high-profile men, where he felt comfortable speaking openly about his addiction.

"Some years later, on April 1, I got sober for what turned out to be the last time," he wrote.

During a conversation with Michael J. Fox for Interview Magazine, Lloyd acknowledged that his struggles with alcohol were not immediately apparent to those around him.

"You accounted in the book that you had alcohol problems," Fox said.

"Yeah, I did," Lloyd replied.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Fox then asked whether Lloyd was drinking while playing his "Taxi" character, Reverend Jim.

"Sometimes," Lloyd said. "It hadn’t gotten to be a big problem yet."

Fox, who has also spoken publicly about his own recovery, asked Lloyd whether it was difficult to share his addiction in the memoir.

"Because once you let it go, it’s out there, and you’re such a private person," Fox said.

"Yeah. I had a problem," Lloyd replied.

"Well, you recovered. We’re both in recovery," Fox responded.

item.title: Inside top Trump bulldog’s plan to save House GOP majority and defy history
item.description: Jim Jordan has barnstormed 115 districts across 34 states this election cycle, raising millions for House Republicans fighting to keep their majority.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, was jumping into the car with his wife on the way to the airport when he took a call from a Fox News Digital reporter on Thursday morning.

It’s a microcosm of what the House Judiciary Committee chairman’s recent weeks and months have been: a seemingly endless series of planes, trains and automobiles across the U.S. campaigning for fellow Republican lawmakers.

House Republicans’ senior leadership is crisscrossing the country raising money and support for their members to win Tuesday’s midterm elections. Jordan, though he’s not part of the trio, has much the same schedule.

"Sometimes they’re fundraisers, sometimes they’re rallies, sometimes they're both," Jordan said. "We're doing everything we can just to help our team win, because… if these Democrats get in there, my real concern, I gotta be honest, is what they're gonna try to do to the structure of our government."

MAPPED: TRUMP’S NONSTOP CAMPAIGN BLITZ SWEEPS KEY STATES

A source familiar with Jordan’s travel schedule said he’ll have gone to 115 districts across 34 states during this election cycle. That includes 19 consecutive days on the road in the lead-up to Nov. 3 in states such as Washington, Oregon, Texas, Arkansas, Florida, Illinois and South Carolina.

And despite the diverse areas, Jordan said his message is mostly the same: Republicans cut taxes, secured the border and Democrats will make it all worse.

"We understand things cost a little too much, and we're working on that. But remember, most of that's because of the Biden administration and their record inflation. We're bringing that inflation rate down, but you know, we still understand things, things cost too much, and we're gonna keep working on that," Jordan said.

TRUMP VOTERS REVEAL THEIR BIGGEST FEAR HEADING INTO MIDTERMS — AND IT'S NOT RISING PRICES

"But the big issue we talk about is, if these radicals that now control the Democrat Party, if they get control of the government, the crazy things they're gonna do are just frightening."

And because he’s not a member of leadership, he’s not afforded the same charter flights and police motorcades that come with that job.

While he’s had some private flights, most of Jordan’s travel has been comprised of commercial airlines and long drives between destinations — including sitting in traffic.

He said his favorite travel tunes include the greatest hits of late country star Glen Campbell.

But Jordan said he also uses much of that time texting or calling colleagues, asking how their races are going, and talking to staff about what issues to raise at his next event.

He’s also raised a significant amount of cash for their campaigns, donating $1.97 million to Republicans across the country and $2.65 million to the House GOP campaign arm.

10 DEMOCRAT-HELD HOUSE SEATS REPUBLICANS COULD FLIP TO SAVE THEIR MAJORITY

It comes as House Republicans fight an uphill battle to retain their majority, as multiple political forecasts show Democrats poised to take over the chamber.

Jordan’s volume of travel is notable for someone who is not in senior House leadership, but it’s not a surprise, given his years-long high profile.

"His celebrity status is very helpful," one House Republican previously told Fox News Digital. "When Jim Jordan comes to town for you, you put 300 butts in seats."

Another lawmaker shared a similar figure. Rep. Tim Moore, R-N.C., told Fox News Digital that Jordan reached out to him about doing an event in his district that wound up a success.

DEMOCRATS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP RED STATES — BUT A $400M GOP SPENDING ADVANTAGE COULD DERAIL THEIR PLANS

"We had a fundraiser in Gastonia and it was very well attended.  A huge crowd, nearly 300 people there — raised a lot of money, a lot of excitement, a lot of enthusiasm, and so I appreciated him coming down to do that," Moore said. His district also saw a visit from House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., which Moore said also raised a significant sum.

Jordan has appeared alongside conservatives in deep red districts and moderates in battlegrounds — walking out to Survivor’s "Eye of the Tiger" for many of those appearances — painting a picture of party unity that’s a far cry from his roots as an anti-establishment rebel leading the House Freedom Caucus.

"It’s kind of a Jordan 2.0," the first House Republican said. "He’s just a great citizen of the conference."

A second House Republican told Fox News Digital that a wide range of members see Jordan as a "mentor." They said Jordan’s travels are a mix of Republicans asking him to come out and him extending those offers himself.

"Jim doesn't care if you're moderate or even if you have to lean left to keep your seat, you have to represent your people," the second House Republican said.

Asked whether he’s changed or the party has, Jordan said it was "the overall picture."

"Any differences that exist in the Republican Party are pretty small compared to the differences between Republicans and the left, the hard left, the radical left, which now controls the Democrat Party," Jordan said.

It has also inspired questions about what he wants out of it.

House Republicans and members of the media are widely expecting that Jordan is eyeing a bid for senior leadership after failing to clinch a position in the past.

If Republicans lose the majority, he’s expected to run for minority leader, where he’d be Trump’s top defender in Congress.

But Jordan himself has publicly dismissed those notions.

"I’m focused on… Tuesday," he told Fox News Digital. "The way you stop the radicals from making these structural changes to our constitutional form of government, these radical policy positions that they have, the way you stop them is at the ballot box, and that happens on Tuesday."

And then the conversation ended, because Jordan had to catch a flight to campaign with Republican candidates in Florida that night.

item.title: US calls Turkey-Libya maritime deal 'unhelpful and provocative' amid regional backlash
item.description: A State Department spokesperson called the Turkey-Libya maritime accord "unhelpful and provocative" as diplomatic tensions escalate in the region.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump State Department denounced the recent eastern Mediterranean maritime agreement between NATO member Turkey and the fractured Libyan state.

The Turkey-Libya deal has also caused frustration and anger among many nations because they say it rewrote the established sea borders of the sensitive Mediterranean Sea region, where large deposits of gas might be located.

The Eastern Libyan parliament approved the maritime accord in mid-October. The region is ruled by military leader Khalifa Haftar, who has formed an alliance with Turkey — the maritime deal ignores Libya’s internationally recognized government in Tripoli in the northwestern part of the oil-rich country. 

A U.S. State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital: "The announcement of the ratification of the Turkish-Libyan delimitation memorandum of understanding has raised tensions in the region and is unhelpful and provocative — and our position on this matter has not changed."

BILLION-DOLLAR POWER LINK CONNECTING ISRAEL TO EUROPE HITS ROADBLOCK IN BITTER REGIONAL FEUD

The spokesperson added: "We encourage all countries, including partners in the Eastern Mediterranean, to resolve maritime disputes through good-faith negotiations and avoid any provocative behavior. Greece and Türkiye are both NATO allies. We encourage them to engage bilaterally to address any areas of disagreement."

According to the spokesperson, "Peaceful resolution of such disputes opens the way for commercial investment and exploration that will benefit the entire region."

According to the Turkish news agency Anadolu Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Wednesday said the maritime agreement between Turkey and Libya was "entirely legitimate" and not in violation of international law.

He added: "This is an entirely legitimate agreement, both from a legal and a political perspective. There is no need to debate it."

Reuters reported Fidan also shot back at critics of the deal. "There are countries reacting to this. We know why they are reacting. Some are doing so because they need to, some really do have strategic problems with this issue. ​ However, this is an entirely legitimate deal, both from a legal and a statutory perspective. ​There is no need to argue this."

NETANYAHU WARNS TURKEY SHOULD NOT GET F-35S, CITING ERDOĞAN'S HOSTILITY TOWARD NATO ALLIES

Fox News Digital sought comment from both Turkey and Libya but did not get a response by time of publication.

Greek Minister of Foreign Affairs George Gerapetritis angrily wrote on his ministry’s website that, "The memorandum will not be implemented. And it will not be implemented for the simple reason that it produces no legal effects whatsoever, as it is entirely contrary to international law." He added, "Türkiye had established a system of influence in Libya, essentially seeking to advance its own interests" and the Turkish media has ramped up its anti-Greece rhetoric. "There is a constant stream of reports pushing the Turkish government to become even more aggressive."

Endy Zemenides, the executive director of the Hellenic American Leadership Council, told Fox News Digital that the Turkey-Libya agreement "absolutely" endangers the security of the U.S. and its allies.

He said: "This memorandum specifically infringes on U.S. companies and U.S. energy policy. It effectively denies maritime rights and zones of Crete. Crete is NATO’s southernmost base. And the U.S. has been increasingly relied upon because of wars in the Mideast." He noted that the American companies Exxon and Chevron are present in Crete.

US-BACKED ISRAEL-MOROCCO DEAL DEEPENS ABRAHAM ACCORDS AMID GROWING REGIONAL THREATS

Zemenides said the Turkey-Libya deal is a way of pushing the U.S. out of the region. The U.S. has not been able to rely on Turkey for a decade, said Zemenides. He continued that "allowing Turkey to challenge the pro-Western order" is not good for American interests.

The European Union invoked unusually strong language targeting the deal, declaring it in violation of maritime law.

"The EU position regarding the MoU is firm and clear. As outlined in the European Council Conclusions of December 2019 and reiterated in June 2025, the Türkiye-Libya Memorandum of Understanding infringes upon the sovereign rights of third States and does not comply with the Law of the Sea. It is null and void and cannot produce any legal consequences for third States."

Israel also blasted Turkey and Libya. The Jewish state has developed a troika alliance with both Greece and Cyprus. Israel’s foreign ministry said on X it "strongly condemns the decision of the Libyan House of Representatives to ratify the Maritime Jurisdiction Memorandum between Turkey and Libya."

Israel’s foreign ministry added on X, "This agreement infringes upon the sovereign rights of our close allies in the region. Regretfully, once again we see Turkey working to destabilize the east Mediterranean region."

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: 5 US destinations named to Best of World travel list for 2027 by National Geographic
item.description: Madison, Wisconsin, leads National Geographic's 2027 Best of the World list, with four other U.S. destinations selected. Choices span from California to Maryland.
item.content:encoded:
Five locations in the U.S. have been chosen by National Geographic as some of the best to travel to in the year ahead.

National Geographic’s annual Best of the World travel list, just released, features 25 travel-worthy destinations all over the globe. 

The five standout U.S. destinations harbor stunning views, great food and unique cultural spaces. 

AMERICANS CHOOSING TO VISIT SMALLER TOWNS OVER BIG CITIES AS TRAVEL COSTS RISE

Check out the details. 

This capital city was listed as the first U.S.-based destination to visit, highlighted for its lakefront adventure opportunities and local cuisine.

Nestled between Lakes Mendota and Monona, Madison, Wisconsin, offers beautiful trails and green spaces. It's also city-central for several colleges, including the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

This mix between college town, nature oasis and state capital gives Madison a unique flare, pairing beloved nightlife spaces with a growing trail network.

National Geographic calls the city of about 290,000 residents "compact enough to explore on foot or by bike," as it’s certified by the League of American Bicyclists.

NY AND LA DIDN'T WIN AMERICA'S BEST MEGA AIRPORT TITLE, BUT ONE MIDWEST HUB DID

Madison reportedly is home to more than 200 miles of hiking trails and bikeways.

These connect neighborhoods, beaches and about 300 parks, which, according to National Geographic, is among the most per capita of any U.S. city.

Bikers can take the 13-mile bike loop around Lake Monona, which passes from the Olbrich Botanical Gardens to Madison’s downtown waterfront.

The Dane County Farmers Market takes place on Saturdays in the summer on Capitol Square, with up to 20,000 visitors. It is reportedly the nation’s largest producer-only market, providing flowers, baked goods and fresh vegetables.

4 US HOTSPOTS JUST MADE NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC'S TOP TRAVEL LIST

National Geographic also shouted out some local restaurants, such as Fairchild for its use of local vegetables in homemade ravioli and Ahan for its classic Laotian dishes.

After mudslides in Big Sur caused a three-year closure, some of the most scenic sections of the Pacific Coast Highway have been reopened, giving travelers the opportunity to take in the inspirational sights of California’s coastline.

"Lesser known artsy communities" lie just outside the roadway, says National Geographic.

On the southern end, artist colony Laguna Beach celebrates its centennial in 2027.

Downtown Laguna Beach not only offers beach access, but fronts a new pedestrian promenade with boutiques, galleries, outdoor performance spaces and "al fresco" dining.

The central-coast city of Lompoc features a trail of more than 30 murals depicting the town’s agricultural roots, as well as a wine region known as the Wine Ghetto.

North of Lompoc is the one-block dairy farmer town of Harmony, which boasts a population of 18. The town features small-batch ice cream at Harmony Valley Creamery, and other locally owned businesses like Harmony Glassworks and Harmony Pottery Studio and Gallery.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The northern end of the highway is home to more artistic regions, like Mendocino County and Fort Bragg, offering exhibitions and galleries like Pacific Textile Arts.

In the heart of the United States, spanning between Missouri and Arkansas, the southern Ozarks show off "spectacular" bluffs, valleys and ridgelines.

The region is a "haven" for outdoor activities, National Geographic said, as well as immerse cultural activities in neighboring towns like Bentonville, Arkansas — home to the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art.

Close to Bentonville, Bella Vista, Arkansas, is the self-proclaimed mountain biking capital of the world, fronting the new OZ Trails Bike Park. It's the state’s first chairlift-served mountain bike park for access to 20 miles of trails for all levels.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

About 60 miles across the Missouri border is Dogwood Canyon Nature Park, where the Ozarks unfold across 10,000 acres, featuring limestone cliffs and valleys, National Geographic detailed.

Herds of elk, bison and longhorn cattle can be spotted here. Visitors can hike and bike the park’s network of trails.

Baltimore is packed with U.S. history as the birthplace of the American railroad.

The port city on the shores of the Chesapeake Bay chartered the country’s first commercial railroad in 1827. The National Museum of Railroad History & Innovation will reportedly mark the 200-year anniversary with a $38 million upgrade.

The museum’s makeover will feature "archival treasures" like letters from Abraham Lincoln and railroad tech exhibits, according to NatGeo.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

National Geographic also highlighted Baltimore’s historic Lexington Market, established in 1782. The public market features merchants like family-owned seafood, produce and baked goods vendors.

Baltimore’s Inner Harbor has attractions like the National Aquarium and 1854 U.S.S. Constellation warship, as well as parks and retail stores. 

The waterfront features a whiskey distillery, green spaces and restaurants offering local delicacy options, like steamed crabs and crab cakes.

The Baltimore Blueway has launched kayaking trails, National Geographic reported. A trip to Fort McHenry also came as a recommendation, as it's the location that inspired Francis Scott Key to write "The Star-Spangled Banner."

National Geographic called attention to a second California location, Catalina Island — a remote destination only accessible by boat.

An hour on the ferry from Long Beach, California, brings visitors to the island's sweeping landscape, including ridgelines and roving bison.

Catalina Island is also home to indigenous plant and animal species, like small foxes that can be spotted along the 38.5 mile Trans-Catalina Trail, and coastal sage shrub.

The Garden to Sky Trail offers an ocean overlook from the Wrigley Memorial and Botanic Garden, which showcases "rare island flora," National Geographic said.
